utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've asked myself whether we should deal with the matter in a situation where all three accused are present, because any conflict of interest with other accused is, in my view, such a private matter that I'd rather discuss it with the Defence of one accused and then with the Defence of another accused, and then with the third accused, so not to do it together, where that is usually done. That's also the reason why I thought that the presence of the three accused, not affected by the issue at all, should not be present. Now, then, the first question is that with whom we would deal first. And at the same time, I could say that the other two accused would not have to wait here any longer, as far as the logistics allow them to be returned to the Detention Unit once they've left this courtroom, they could be transported back to the Detention Unit. Perhaps -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe we could be first, in view of the fact that we have to leave The Hague tomorrow. I would be willing and ready, if possible, to start, to be first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, I couldn't promise you that we would finish the matter with you, whereas I see the problems seem to be less in respect of Mr. Jonjic and Mr. Coric. So therefore, I'm quite willing to start with you, but I couldn't guarantee that we'll finish by -- within ten minutes. Is it still your preference to -- yes. Okay. Then I would like to ask the security to ask Mr. -- Let me now see - Mr. Coric and Mr. Prlic to be transported back to the Detention Unit. I expect to see you back tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SALAHOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm making a mistake. I apologise. Of course not. Because Mr. Prlic should stay. I apologise for making the mistake. And Mr. -- yes, Mr. Stojic and Mr. Coric would then leave at this moment. I hope to see you back tomorrow. Later in the morning, I expect to deal with the issue finally with you. Yes. And then Mr. Prlic would stay for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Other Defence counsel do not have to stay. They're free to do whatever they think fit, of course. It's a public hearing, so I'm not chasing you out, but if you want to use your time as efficiently as possible, then please feel free to leave this courtroom. And let me just check. I would like to ask a few questions to your counsel, Mr. Prlic, to find out whether there's any confusion, yes or no. Let me first try to check the following: Is it true that Mr. Prlic is charged with the same acts committed in Mostar municipality between April 1993 and April 1994, the same acts for which Mr. Martinovic stood trial and is now on appeal? I do understand that Mr. Martinovic was from May to September 1993 and that in the present indictment, it's April 1993 and April 1994. Do we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me put the following question to you: You have said that the case against Mr. Martinovic will be ended soon, and therefore, the risk of a conflict of interest is not that relevant or not that important. And you said his case would be finished prior to the start of the trial against Mr. Prlic. Is that a correct understanding of at least part of your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This is what I have stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Don't you think that the Defence of Mr. Prlic starts now, and not only at trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that the defence of Jadranko Prlic started with his Initial Appearance. Would you like me to elaborate on that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like then to better understand your position where you say, well, Mr. Martinovic's trial will be ended soon, and that's at least before the trial against Mr. Prlic will start, so there's in this respect not a real problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try and explain. I may have not been very precise. The truth is that I was referring to the period that will elapse before the beginning of trial, and the beginning of defence is different. It is my position that in the stage of the Vinko Martinovic case, my defence and the defence of Vinko Martinovic have been defined. We have now reached the stage in which the defence has been finalised and brought to an end. Bearing that in mind, at the same time, I am familiar with the defence of Mr. Jadranko Prlic. I know the elements of this defence that we can not discuss at the moment. I have spoken about that, both with Mr. Prlic and with Mr. Martinovic. When I asked Mr. Vinko Martinovic: What do you think Vinko -- the first question, my question to him was: How did he feel about this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. engagement. And then I asked him for his opinion about a possible conflict of interest. In other words, whether my engagement in this case would be detrimental to his rights. And this is what he told me, literally: I support you. Do whatever you want to do, because my case will end before his case starts. Inspired by that sentence of his, I may have misspoken when I said that one trial will end and the other will not have started. My position is as follows: One procedure starts, one defence has completed. Being familiar with the guidelines and directions of both defences and having spoken with both clients, bearing in mind the charges against, I do not see a link between the two cases and I do not see a situation in which the defence of one would be at the detriment of the other. Bearing all that in mind and having all this information, I am now appearing in this Tribunal as counsel for two accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me put the following question to you. Let's just assume, for argument's sake, that Mr. Martinovic will be convicted for having committed certain acts. Let's also assume that the Court, the Chamber - I don't know what Chamber it will be, but the Chamber would take judicial notice of the acts of Mr. Martinovic. Would you still feel free to defend, for example, for Mr. Prlic, that he was unaware of what happened and, therefore, it is rather Mr. Martinovic that should have received a high sentence because committing these kind of things without proper reporting to higher-up officials is something really bad? Would you feel free to follow such a line of defence, if it would be established that Mr. Martinovic ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure that I have understood your question correctly. At this moment, I don't see such a possibility. I simply don't see that, because I have spoken with both of my clients about that. My position towards my clients is as follows: Vinko Martinovic is my personal client -- my principal client in this case. I had Vinko Martinovic's authority, authorisation, from the very beginning of his trial, and I'm not going to betray that trust in any case. And before I started representing Mr. Jadranko Prlic, I told him that, and I also told him that I would never put him in a situation not to use something that I could use from the Martinovic case and that would be of use to him. If I were to find myself in such a position, Your Honour, rest assured that I will not do harm by any of my clients. Why do I believe that? In this case, I am a co-counsel. I'm not the creator of Mr. Prlic's defence. The defence of Mr. Prlic is created by the lead counsel and Mr. Jadranko Prlic himself. I don't have the power to influence that defence. However, for the sake of the argument, if such a hypothetical situation should arise, I am willing to withdraw from this case. And these were the elements that I had in mind when I decided to participate in the defence of Mr. Jadranko Prlic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand you well that you say: My primary loyalty is to Mr. Martinovic, and if I would know something which I should not make known to Mr. Prlic, then I would rather withdraw then, because my primary loyalty is to Mr. Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am equally loyal to both clients. We cannot talk about my being more loyal to one than to the other. I'm equally loyal to both. If I were put in the position to harm one of the clients in my role, I would inform that client and I would withdraw from that case. I believe that both my cases are equal, equally valid, and I do not see any difference between the two clients. I mention Mr. Vinko Martinovic as my principal client because I started with him, but that doesn't mean that the loyalty of Mr. Jadranko Prlic does not give me the same obligation and that I'm not facing the same level of commitment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then explain exactly what you meant when you said: "I had Vinko Martinovic's authority, authorisation, from the very beginning of his trial, and I'm not going to betray that trust in any case. And before I start representing Mr. Jadranko Prlic, I told him that, and I also told him that I would never put him in a situation not to use something that I could use from the Martinovic case and that would be of use to him." Now, you know something from the Martinovic case. Mr. Martinovic told you confidentially, gave you confidentially certain information. Would you use it in the case? Because from your words, I do understand that you would use it from the case for Mr. Prlic as well or otherwise clarify what exactly you meant by those words.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What did I mean, Your Honour? I meant simply: I would not betray any of my clients. I meant specifically that if there is a secret I am bound by lawyer/client privilege. Every client is special. I cannot choose between two clients. If Vinko Martinovic confided in me and imparted some information, that information is protected by a lawyer/client privilege. That is my personal ethics and my professional ethics. I will never betray that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now the following situation. Let's again, for argument's sake and for nothing else: Mr. Martinovic tells you they could never prove that, but, as a matter of fact, I did never act upon orders. I neglected all my orders. But whatever I did, Mr. Prlic could not have known about it, but I'll just deny that I ever did anything at all. What would you do in that situation? Because that could be very interesting information for Mr. Prlic, isn't it, confidentially given to you by Mr. Martinovic, which you could not use, in the interest of Mr. Prlic, where it would be highly disculpatory [phoen] for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would deal with that very simply, together with Mr. Martinovic. I would simply ask him: Why are you telling me this? Are you telling me this in the context of our relationship? Do you want me to impart that information, to divulge it, or do you want to address the Court, or what? Depending on what he answers, I would act accordingly. If he tells me, "I'm telling this to you as my lawyer," that remains buried as a secret between us. If he tells me he wants that information to go further --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if Mr. -- it could certainly help Mr. Prlic, then, isn't it? So you have to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that piece of information that Vinko Martinovic would hypothetically give me were something protected by lawyer/client privilege, even if it were useful to Jadranko Prlic, I would not share it with Jadranko Prlic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's for sure. And you would even, having this information, you would be limited in your investigations to find out the specific responsibility of Mr. Prlic, isn't it? Because you couldn't go against this information to start investigating, because Mr. Martinovic would say to you: Well, I told you in confidence what I knew, and now you're not using that, but you're exactly exploring and investigating in that direction. So that's against the loyalty you owe to me, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under no circumstances would I investigate based on that information. I have a lot of information linked to a number of clients, and I view each set of information individually. I never take the position of representing several clients and making trade-offs between different sets of information. And generally, I have reservations about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like to continue tomorrow morning, because we haven't got sufficient time to explore all the details of it. I'd like to see -- Mr. Par and Mr. Prlic, I'd like to see you back tomorrow morning, continue with you, and then I'd like to continue with you, Mr. Olujic, if I now pronounce it well, and Mr. Jonjic, in respect of their clients. We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning. Would you please try to find out time and place. Presumably it will be Trial Chamber -- the Courtroom I at 2.00 -- Courtroom II. Yes. Even -- well, we have no Prosecution present, so Courtroom II is a very small one, but the three of you will fit in. So Courtroom II. And is the time known already, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is somebody asking me?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It seems around 11.00, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, not earlier than 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 11.00 is all right with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: adjourned at 7.13 p.m.
